translations.text: Those who do improper things among us—this is how we bring shame on the good people among us who do good, we who do evil.
Oh, how clearly we show that we are lovers of sin!
Noah was righteous and innocent, living among those who had abandoned God.
Yet we ourselves sin in the midst of those who have left sin behind, to do [?]
Lot lived with people more wicked than anyone else. And
we live
For many among all the saints, down to Daniel and his companions, lived in the midst of godless people. They kept themselves holy and did not sin.
Yet we ourselves sin in the midst of those who love God. We gather together with them, and we all pronounce the name of God and his angels. We also speak about the saints.
We also speak and listen, we who are unworthy: “I appeal to the elders among you as a fellow elder and a witness to the sufferings of Christ.”
We get angry with anyone who tells us, “You do not know God or his law.” Yet we ourselves do godless deeds.
What, then, will we say in the face of these words: “Everyone who sins has neither seen him nor known him”?
Is not the tree [?]? Not only does it bend beneath its fruit, but it also carries it.
Is it not written, “Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire”?
If the saints and our fathers, the prophets and the apostles, and all the righteous said about themselves:
Jews and Greeks, our honorable deeds have become a laughingstock. And again: “O man, Jesus is the truth.”
Do not look to me, but to Jesus. Do not call anyone on earth your teacher. As for what I am going to do, you have no business with me.
You are not slaves of human beings. You were bought for a price. Jesus is the one who gave his blood; he is your Lord.
And again: “Perhaps some people, when they hear me, will say, ‘I will go out and rob.’ For someone who teaches is like someone who urges others on.”

For perhaps you are secretly [?]: “If the opportunity comes to the person saying these things, he will become even greedier and take advantage of others.” And you would not be mistaken in saying this.
But again, because there are people who hate, and people who are always looking for fault with those who speak the truth, he said, “We have said enough. We have spoken openly.”
Let whoever hates go on hating. Let whoever is distressed go on being distressed. For we will give an account to God, where there is no favor or money that can set aside the truth.
He said these things not only about you who are in the house [?] God, but also when he saw that evil had increased on the earth,
especially oppression because of the love of money. Instead of saying, “We will go to God as better or good people,”
he said, “We will go in a worse state than when we came. For we brought no possessions when we came, and we had neither sins nor possessions.”
But now the possessions will remain here, along with all the other empty desires. Our sins, however, will go ahead of us, come with us, and follow us.
But who can speak of the perfection of that man of God, and of all his words, which contain no hypocrisy
or flattery toward oppressive people, any pagan, any sect, or any people who are not upright?
For we will give an account to God, where there is no favor or money that can set aside the truth.
He said these things not only about you who are in the house [?] God, but also when he saw that evil had increased on the earth,
especially oppression because of the love of money. Instead of saying, “We will go to God as better or good people,”
he said, “We will go in a worse state than when we came. For we brought no possessions when we came, and we had neither sins nor possessions.”
But now the possessions will remain here, along with all the other empty desires. Our sins, however, will go ahead of us, come with us, and follow us.
[?] When we take on the titles “ruler” and “authority,” each according to his kind, and we all boast in the great things of God
and in his holy places, we do not know what will confront us when we give an account to God for all our deeds. If only we would not be even more
Be ashamed, and let us grieve on that day, for I will not say, “Let us lament and weep,” in the place where the friendships [?] in vain.
There is a person who rejoices when he receives necessary goods entrusted to him, and who gives them back with confidence to the person who entrusted them to him when that person asks him for them.
And is anyone happy when he stretches out to receive the things that have been [?] to him? No, for he becomes gloomy and grieves.
He is also afraid because he has not guarded the things entrusted to him. Instead, they drag him to the places of judgment, covered in shame and afraid.
But he is again full of turmoil, not thinking of [?] these things that you hear, O man who looks ahead to the place
of judgment in heaven. And I too understood what the one who reveals things to those worthy of them was saying:
“If I too am concerned about standing before Christ’s judgment seat.” Not everyone is recognized as trustworthy when receiving something. Rather, the real test is the time for giving back
what you received, and for proving yourself faithful because you have handed it back to the one who gave it to you, with nothing missing.
A person will inquire and investigate who is trustworthy enough to be entrusted with perishable earthly possessions. Someone examines him before he receives them,
to see whether he will safeguard what has been entrusted to him. And will those who receive high positions from God fail to examine them?
And will those through whom the name is received fail to examine them—what they are, what sort of people they are, and their other deeds?
How will anyone say that [?] exists [?] all of them [?] saying:
Rather, these things that you hear, O man.
Not everyone is recognized as trustworthy when receiving something. Rather, the real test is the time for giving back what you received,
and for proving yourself faithful because you have handed it back to the one who gave it to you, with nothing missing.
A person will inquire and investigate who is trustworthy enough to be entrusted with perishable earthly possessions. Someone examines him before he receives them,
to see whether he will safeguard what has been entrusted to him. And will those who receive high positions from God fail to examine them?
And will those through whom the name is received fail to examine them—what they are, what sort of people they are, and their other deeds?
How will anyone say that [?] exists [?] all of them [?] saying:
Those who do those abominable deeds in the holy places are themselves traitors, thieves, and apostates.
What use are many lamps placed on lampstands if they do not burn because they are no good?
Likewise, that of the holy and faithful people who live in it.
A person who is of no use to himself and does not benefit himself—how will he be useful for a necessary task? Or is there an honored title that will benefit him? Judas was of no use to himself alone.
For a necessary task.
That apostate, while the Lord says, 'If a person gains the whole world and loses his soul,'
What will he give in exchange for his soul?
To give himself over to a trap of the devil.
As for money, if only gold had never existed! Yet we also accept it gladly when God gives it to us for a need.
But to incur that judgment because of it is lawlessness. If only gold had never existed! Then they would not have sold the righteous person for silver, and [?]
If only gold had never existed, and they would have handed over the righteous person
at all times, and to plant.
Or to bring people in to them who will recognize the favor of the one who honored them.
a ship. Watch the rat’s tooth, so that we too may guard our hearts with every precaution, as it is written, against every
evil thing that breaks into it or whispers thoughts to it that destroy the heart and soul of the people who accept them.
For it was because of these things that it was said, “They committed sexual immorality in the thoughts of their hearts.” These are the things that lead to downfall,
as it is written, “Evil thoughts precede downfall.” It was because of these things that it was said, “A lying spirit stood up and poured out wine and drunkenness for you.”
For through these things, people of this sort come out to wage war against one another with these weapons of conflict, namely:
jealousy, hatred, slander, insults, spite, and things like these. This is how Satan devises
many dark things against one another, until they make themselves liable to God’s judgment. For those whom he has made enemies of true righteousness are beyond counting.
In these ways, with a love mixed with jealousy and hatred, this is how we will be put to shame on the day when God judges people’s secrets.
How will we hide our jealousy and our hatred toward one another on that day? Who will raise a staff against his neighbor—
not to mention a sword and a spear—without being seen? [?] But as for us, who will think, or who will suspect, that we are stabbing one another with all these things, when they see
how we speak to one another with every peaceful word, while hostility is in our hearts? It is better not to seek one another’s well-being with malice.
in our hearts, rather than greeting hypocritically and with false love. Do not ask whether I am well or whether I am making progress

in goodness. Nor should you rejoice because you have heard that what you want is happening to me. Do not say, “He will live a long time.” Nor should you rejoice because you have heard that he has died.
What will this human glory do for us? Let us feel ashamed before these words: “The Lord knows that human thoughts are empty.” My coming
is not into your hands, so that I should be afraid or ashamed for you to discover that there are evil things in my heart against you. Nor are you coming
into my hands, so that you should be afraid or ashamed for me to hear that you speak evil against me. Rather, we are coming into God's hands. We are blessed,
not because we bear a name while we are full of malice toward one another, but we are blessed if the Savior Jesus saves us from Satan's evil, this malicious deceit
that is in a person's heart against his neighbor. We sit at the same table. I eat bread with you. Your hand is in the dish with mine. We live together in the holy places.
You are at the altar with me. I stand beside the table with you. I place the body of Christ in your hands. You offer
me his blood, while our hearts are full of evil toward one another. And we do not fear the wrath and the curse that came down upon those of former times
who were defiled by evils like these. Were these things written for nothing? Did they not know that there would always be many people going about in God's house
whose hearts were not upright toward one another? Whoever wants to know about evils like these and understand their repayment—look, they are written in the Psalms,
which say about the people who committed them, “Let death come upon them. Let them go down alive into Hades.” But do not distort what we are saying.
For there is a difference between the holy people in God's house who are distressed and find fault with those who do evil among them, so that
they regard them as enemies, and those whose hearts are full of malice and hostility toward one another. These words were not written for nothing, nor merely
about those who went about in God's house in former times, whose hearts were not upright toward one another, or about Judas alone: “The one who eats
my bread has raised his heel against me,” or, “He used to eat meals with me,” and the other sayings like these. Rather, they were written
about those who would always go about deceitfully in the holy places, whose hearts were not upright toward God, and whose hearts were not upright
toward one another. Where is Judas now? He is in Hades. Why? Because of theft and betrayal. His hand was in the dish
with God, while he was ready to betray him. But let us fear Gehenna and be ashamed of ourselves,
we who have received God's name and honors. Let us keep ourselves holy, free from the deeds of Judas in God's house.
For that man committed these still greater evils because it was after he had received the bread that Satan entered him. This great wrath justly came down upon him,
in keeping with the wickedness of his deeds, because, instead of his being cleansed of Satan by receiving some of the bread that the Lord broke and gave him,
Satan entered him all the more. This is how he quickly crossed over to the other side: instead of being an apostle, he became a devil. You see that whoever makes room
within himself for the unclean spirit, after receiving grace, after receiving the name, after putting on the habit,
will go on to commit many evils. Did we not leave the home of our worldly life to avoid sin? And where do these deeds of darkness and perversity come from?
Thorns and thistles will close in on us, or we will become entangled in them, along with our foolishness and our negligence, which have made bitter things sweet to us.
I am speaking of impurities, defilements, and sexual immorality of every kind, things utterly remote from the rules of honorable marriage
and foreign to the undefiled marriage bed; and of envy, hatred, slander, greed, and favoritism
in judgment, and all the other things with which we have filled God's places. They are traps and snares for us, and stones and pits,
so that we become entangled in them, stumble over them as well, and fall into them. Who else is charged
with separating the holy from the defiled, and the bad from the good, as much as the person in God's house? For those who desire what is good will act according to what they see us doing,
and evildoers will act according to what they see us doing, and will go even further. The unclean
is not only a defiled person who is separated from a holy person. Nor is the defiled only something unsuitable to be offered as a sacrifice to the Lord,
which is separated from what is pure according to the commandments. Rather, every evil thing, from crooked judgments to hypocrisy, is unclean.
Anyone who touches these things—that is, who does them—will become unclean before God unless he withdraws from them, just as
all sins are impurities in the eyes of truly godly people. This is why judges who are not upright are called
'unclean,' because of their unclean deeds, and upright judges are called 'clean,' because of their righteous deeds and their just judgments.
It is the same with someone who dishonors a good person while honoring an evil person, and insults a righteous person in front of an ungodly person.
The heart within him is unclean, especially since he is like someone who blocks
a spring of water. Who will say that this is not so, except someone who has within him what God detests—pride—as it is written in the Gospel? Or shall we entertain
these proud thoughts, I saying, 'As if you were going to guide me!' and you saying, 'As if this man were going to teach me!' Yet we have not mourned over our sins,
so that God may not cast us away from him on the day of our distress. Or are these not human beings to whom he will say at that time, 'Depart
from me,' or, 'I do not know you or who you are'? What shall we say at that time? Shall we say, 'In your name
we received positions of authority or high rank; in your name we clothed ourselves in religious garments; in your name we lived in your holy places; in your name we read the Scriptures'?
Those people too will say, 'In your name we prophesied, and in your name we cast out demons, and in your name we performed many miracles.'
But they will gain nothing. Why, then, have they forgotten their deeds? If he will say to these people, 'Depart from me, you who are cursed,'
Into the fire forever, because they did not do what he said. Then how much greater is our woe, since we destroy essential works, namely God's ordinances and what is right!
on the day when God judges people's secrets, shall we conceal our envy and our hatred toward one another?
How could we, on that day? Who will raise a club against his neighbor—not to mention a sword and a spear—and not be seen?
[?] into your hands because I am afraid or ashamed to let you know that there are evil thoughts against you in my heart. Nor are you coming
into my hands because you are afraid or ashamed to let me hear that you speak evil against me. Rather, we are coming into God's hands naked.
not because we bear a name while we are full of malice toward one another. Rather, blessed are we if the Savior Jesus saves us from Satan’s evil, this deceit of strife,
which is in a person’s heart toward his neighbor. We sit at the same table; I eat bread with you; your hand is in the bowl with mine. We live together in the holy places.
You are at the altar with me. I stand beside the table with you. I place the body of Christ in your hands; you give me in return
his blood. Our hearts are full of evil toward one another, and we do not fear the wrath and the curse that came upon those of former times,
who were blinded by such evils. Were these things written for no purpose?
No, for many will walk at all times.
He is in Hades. Why? Because of theft and betrayal. His hand is in the bowl with God, while he is ready to betray him.
And
It is not only an unclean person who is separated from a holy person.
Nor is it only an unclean thing, unsuitable to be offered as a sacrifice to the Lord, that is separated from what is clean, according to the commandments.
[?] these arrogant attitudes: I, for my part, say, “As if you were the one to guide me!” And you say, “As if this man were the one to teach me!” Yet we have not mourned over our sins,
so that God will not cast us away from him on the day of our distress. Or are they not human beings too, those to whom he will say at that time, “Depart
from me,” or, “I do not know you or who you are”? What will we say at that time? Will we say, “In your name
we received offices or positions of authority; in your name we clothed ourselves in religious habits; in your name we lived in your holy places, reading the Scriptures”?
Into the fire forever, because they did not do what he said. Then how much greater is our woe, since we destroy essential works, namely God's ordinances and what is right!
And the work of his hands—I am speaking of our bodies, each one individually—
just as he made the members of Christ into the members of a prostitute, along with every work of the devil. But I will express this statement another way and explain it as a sign of the wrath

that will come upon everyone who oppresses the poor. For if Jesus, when he comes, will say to those who did not feed him when he was hungry, did not give him a drink when he was thirsty, and did not clothe him when he was naked,
“Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire,” then those who plundered the houses of the poor and made them miserable,
robbing them and taking the fruits of their labor, though they have no claim against them—how much more will he curse them! He will justly say to them, “Even if you did not give them anything
to eat or to wear, why do you take away even the bread they have? Why do you leave them naked, stripping off even the clothing they wear?” They compared
the person who hates his brother to a murderer. It was for this deed that the Lord God cast Cain out of his presence. And it is astonishing that we are not afraid
as we hate one another, when Scripture says, “The father of a person who seeks wisdom will rejoice.” If we hear that our children,
or those who follow us in rank, though not in our deeds, are speaking words of God,
or have done good deeds, we are distressed because we do not want anyone to say, “Someone else has done something good,”
but instead say, “There is no one else like us.” This is what gives rise to every kind of envy. Because of this Cain rose against Abel and killed him. Because of this Joseph was sold as a slave.
Because of this the Jews opposed what Paul was saying,
speaking slanderously. It is no wonder if Christians suffer at the hands of pagans or heretics because they envy them,
just as the Philistines afflicted Isaac because they envied him, and just as all the people of God have endured every kind of distress from the beginning until now
because of all the godless people. But it is far more astonishing that we envy one another, afflict one another, and hand one another over to death,
since we have one and the same God. There is another thing that harms fathers and brings ruin to children, namely this:
so that those in authority honor people to make them follow them, or appoint them to necessary tasks of God, while hearing
and knowing about their evil deeds; and so that disobedient children and every undisciplined person hate those who tell them the truth.
because of all the godless people. But it is all the more astonishing that we envy one another, cause one another suffering, and hand one another over to death, although we have one and the same God.
And he killed them in his anger because they did not stop.
Not.
There are things that a person incurs no sin by not vowing to do. For the Lord said, “Whoever is able to bear it,
let him bear it.” But if he vows to do them and does not do them, woe to him! These are: remaining a virgin, taking up your cross, following God,
serving as a priest in his house, and becoming a monk. Whoever, then, falls away from these things or turns back from them has himself denied him,
and has become a pillar of salt like Lot’s wife—that is, a person with no wisdom in him. If we say, “These words fight against us,”
Even if they [?]
he, for his part, would not have settled in the corners, the streets, and the surroundings of your house. You are the one who showed him the paths for coming in
and going out deceitfully. You are the one who hid him [?] in your heart, your soul, and your mind, like a woman who has hidden the man
committing adultery with her in the storerooms and the corners of her house. You are the one who brought him to the place where the treasure is hidden. You are the one who pointed it out to him.
Search, you foolish virgin! Look through all your belongings, so that you may know what he has not taken from what belongs to you. Your purity is the great
treasure. Your prayer is the bracelet and the various rings on your hands and fingers. Your walking in freedom is the anklets on your feet.
Your obedience is the earring in your ears. Your humility is the ring and the necklace of [?] around your neck. Your knowledge is
the adornment on your head or around your forehead. Your fasts are the bridles of your body. Your meditations on the word of God are
the covering of your feet. Your good deeds are the fine clothes you put on. Grace is the perfume
and the oil with which you anoint yourself and which you put on your head. Truth is the belt you fasten around yourself. Wisdom is the cloak
you wrap around yourself. Are these and the others the things he has not taken from you entirely, down to the eye paint? He scraped it out of its containers;
he took it: the modesty, or the good sense of shame, in your eyes. That woman said to her brother, “I will hold you
and bring you into my mother’s house and into the chamber of her who conceived me.” So now the virgin who is truly
guarding for herself all her wealth in the good deeds she has done in her youth prays
that Jesus and his Spirit may dwell in her. You, however, seized an enemy and brought him into your house and your chamber.
You welcomed the abominable and unclean spirit, but withdrew from the holy and beloved one, the good Spirit—not
because he cannot save, but rather because he handed you over to the one who hates you, because you loved strangers and followed them.
You loved those who sleep with you, and increased your prostitution with them. You multiplied those who are far from you, so that they might live with you in your house.
I am speaking of the spirit of wickedness and the world rulers of darkness, and also the ungodly people who have become this single mixture with you,
and you with them, you miserable soul! But as for your God and your Lord Jesus, do not abandon him.
The fine clothes you usually wear. Your grace is
Because you loved strangers and followed them, you loved those who sleep with you.
And you increased their sexual immorality with them. You multiplied those who were far from you, so that they settled in their house with you. I am speaking of the spirit of wickedness,
and the world rulers of darkness, and also the ungodly people who entered into this same union with you, and you with them, you miserable soul.
You were in their hearts and in their thoughts, as it is written. He too, when he saw you, disregarded you, and you did not fear him.
He too will declare his righteousness, and the wind will carry you away, along with all those attached to you, their deeds, and their glory. A storm
will destroy them. Let us stop, then, engaging in these deeds through which we stir up the anger of God's wrath against us. How long, then, will we speak to God hypocritically,
and spread out our hands deceitfully before the one from whom the ugliness of our deeds is not hidden?
How long will these afflictions remain on the earth because of our acts of oppression and all the things that none of us wants done to himself, yet we do
to one another? “Remove the sins, and I will remove the sufferings, the scourges, and the afflictions from you,” says this voice, which says, “Remove
these evil things from your hearts, from before my eyes. Stop your wickedness.” How long will we disgrace ourselves
and dishonor ourselves, along with our other good things? Who will defile or pollute the Lord's ordinances
without first defiling himself and polluting his deeds? I cannot say anything without having to give an account for it. Therefore I tell you
that there is someone reading the Scriptures or singing psalms of whom they say in heaven, “The one whose mouth deserves to be shut!” There is someone
in the holy places, also clothed in the honored name, of whom they say in the heavens, “The enemy of God's houses,
and the one whose robe deserves to be torn off him!” There is someone approaching the altar and receiving the Lord's body and blood, of whom they say in heaven,
“The one whose hands and feet deserve to be cut off!” There is a man, there is a woman, whom people on earth think of as lights in complete purity,
but of whom they say in heaven, “Look, people who are unclean in everything!” There will certainly be a judgment between those who hear these words with sighs
and tears, and those who hear them with grumbling and murmuring—if indeed they do not hate the one who rebukes them. This name
and this robe—what will they do for us while we engage in these improper deeds? It is through the word spoken by the prophet that we will become rich,
namely: “Let the gentle person become a warrior. Let the one who has no strength say, ‘I am strong.’” Against whom is the gentle person to become a warrior,
or in what is he to become strong? Let him fight for the truth and for God's judgments. Let him fight against sin. Let him become strong and oppose the glory
that is empty, hypocrisy, favoritism, and fear of other people—especially rich oppressors
and godless pagans. Anyone who hears these words but pays no attention to his sins is someone who does not think about his end
and the hour of his distress. Anyone who finds fault with the person saying these things is someone whose inner thoughts have been covered over by wickedness and arrogance,
as it is written. Everything that does not benefit us at the hour of our distress is a loss to our souls. In what did those who came excel in wisdom
from a great distance to this place to make inquiries or pass judgment about possessions that have been stolen. A person whose task it is [?] specks from the eyes
of people, where they destroy their light—how is it not foolishness on his part if he throws out the specks and leaves beams in them? I say this because, if
I am here exposing people because they have stolen possessions, or passing judgment on them, why should I not expose them because sin has stolen them,
and pass judgment on them and show them the places where the enemy has hidden them, namely, defilement, impurity, and every sin?
The purpose of this place is for us to benefit our soul, which the whole world is not worth. Do not let anyone come to me about such a matter. I
am not that sort of person. If there is someone you know who understands the things you are seeking, like the prophets and apostles, go to those people.
But have they come to know themselves, that they should know the things you will go to them about? If you do go to them, you will not find mercy
before God because of them. It is not the world, brothers, that has filled us with deception; rather, we have filled it. Therefore, it is time to become wise.
Do not let anyone make fools of you, for there are many deceivers making fools of many people through these practices. No person
who fears God will say such things, even if they really know. The great prophet Moses was in the midst of the darkness and the cloud,
and God spoke with him, so that nothing was hidden from him. Yet he never said anything like this, nor did any of the other saints:
“Go to such-and-such a place, and you will find possessions that have been stolen,” or, “This is who took them,” as those who deceive many people now do, though they know
nothing. Rather, they said, “Every matter will be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses,” or the stolen goods must be found in the possession of those who took them. As the end
of every dispute, he said, “An oath before God shall be between them.” Even if Samuel said to Saul,
“Your donkeys have been found,” what does this matter have to do with the things you say? Saying, “Who stole some possessions?” is very different from saying, “They have been found.”
Is not saying, “They have been found,” a peaceful matter? It is another thing to say, “Here is where they are,” or, “This is who took them,” as is done now
by those who stir you up to hostility and other troubles, while you cause disturbances in the houses of those about whom they told you, “They
are the ones who took them.” You gain nothing except lies, fighting, and hatred toward one another. But since we have spoken of joy
and heard of joy, I will finish with these things: may the God of all compassion make us worthy of these two things, so that we may share in everything,
namely, that he protect the innocent among his people, and that he also set us sinners right, freeing us from every lawless act, and not hide his face from us from today onward,
from the day we resolved in our hearts to keep his words, so that we too may hear this encouragement through this declaration,
like those of that time: “I will bring you out from the nations and gather you from the whole earth,
and bring you into your land. I will sprinkle pure water upon you”—that is, the perfect word of the Scriptures—
“and you will be cleansed from all your impurities and from all your idols.
I will purify you.” And again: “I will establish a covenant of peace with them, and it will be a covenant for them. I will establish them and multiply them.”
and I will place my sanctuary among them forever, and my dwelling will be over them. And again: “I will bring Jacob back from captivity, and I will have mercy
on the whole house of Israel.” And again: “From now on I will no longer leave them in that place”—he is speaking of their enemies’ land—“and I will not hide my face
from them, because I have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel,” says Adonai, the Lord. I said these things knowing that you want to hear them.
Rather, I remember how I saw your tears flowing over your cheeks when this least of men
said this: “Do we go up onto the chair or the throne to read aloud to those who listen to the word of God
in his churches, or do we instead go down into pits?” And again: “What wisdom does a shepherd have
if he draws water and gives a flock of sheep water to drink, but does not himself give a ewe of his own anything to drink? Or again, someone who has lit
many lamps in other people’s houses but does not light his own in his chamber?” And because you are wise and have understood
how to do these things for him, while we in turn do them for one another: “Remove the sins, and I will remove the hardships, the scourges, and the afflictions from you,” said this voice
that says: “Remove these wicked deeds from your hearts, from before my eyes. Stop your wickedness,” until we see that we are bringing shame on ourselves.
For they are lights in every kind of purity, while it is said of them in heaven, “Look, they are impure in everything.”
And greed spreads a covering over the thoughts within his heart, as it is written: “Everything that does not benefit us in the time of our need is harmful to our souls.”
But if they recognized themselves, they would know what you are going to them about.
Because they have found glory. What does this matter have to do with the things you are saying?
“And I will gather you from the whole earth and bring you into your land. I will sprinkle pure water over you”—that is, the complete word of the Scriptures—
“and you will be cleansed of all your impurities and of all your idols.
And I will purify you.” And again: “I establish a covenant of peace with them, and they will have a covenant,
and I will give them and multiply them, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever, and my dwelling will be over them.”
Or the throne, reading aloud to those who listen to the word of God.

Christ. Those who commit those abominable deeds in the holy places are themselves traitors, thieves, and apostates.

Adam and Eve quickly recognized the shame of the offense they had committed, and they did not take long to realize that they were naked. That is why they looked for something to cover it.
And so they plucked fig leaves and made themselves loincloths from them, for they were troubled and ashamed.
But we, who persist in our sins all the time, have not recognized the shame of our sins. Nor have we realized that we are stripped of the glory that used to cover us before we sinned.
That is why we do not concern ourselves with accepting commandments and doing the things commanded us in the Scriptures, so that we may cover our shame.
If a barbarian invades a land or a region, where will its inhabitants flee to be safe, except to the fortified cities?
But if they take control of the strongholds, where will the people go? Perhaps those who are able will flee up into the mountains and be safe.
Likewise, if Satan attacks souls to deceive them and kill them through evil,
to whom will they flee except those in positions of authority in the house of God, so that they may teach them the skills of warfare and the weapons of battle, and they may overcome sin?
But if we are the first to grow weak, or if we fall into evil when the enemy places stumbling blocks at our feet, where will the people go? Or who will help them?

For through these things, people of this kind go out to wage war against one another with these weapons of conflict: jealousy, hatred, slander,
insults, mockery, and things like these. This is how Satan devises much darkness within us against one another, until they make themselves liable to God’s judgment.
For countless are those whom he has made enemies of true righteousness in these ways, through a love mixed with jealousy
and hatred. This is how we will be put to shame on the day when God judges people’s secrets.
How will we hide our jealousy and our hatred toward one another on that day? Who can raise a club against his neighbor—not to mention a sword or an axe—without being seen?
But as for us, who will suspect, or who will accuse us of stabbing one another with all these things, when they see how we speak to one another
with every peaceful word, while hostility is in our hearts? It is better not to ask after one another’s well-being, with no malice in our hearts, than to ask with hypocrisy and a false love.
Do not ask whether I am well or whether I am making progress in goodness. And do not rejoice because you have heard of the things you want to happen to me.
Do not say, “May he live a long time,” and then rejoice because you have heard that he has died. What good will this human honor do us?
Let us feel shame before these words: “The Lord knows people’s thoughts, that they are empty.”
I am not going to fall into your hands because I am afraid or ashamed for you to know that there are evil things in my heart against you. Nor are you going to fall
into my hands because you are afraid or ashamed for me to hear that you speak evil against me. Rather, we are going to fall into God’s hands.
We are not blessed because we bear a name while we are full of malice toward one another. Rather, we are blessed if Jesus the Savior rescues us from Satan’s evil:
that ancient deceit in a person’s heart against his neighbor. We sit at the same table. I eat bread with you. Your hand is in the bowl with mine.
We live together in the holy places. You are at the altar with me. I stand beside the table with you. I place the body of Christ into your hand.
You pour out his blood for me. Our hearts are full of evil toward one another, and we do not fear the wrath and the curse that came upon those before us who became entangled in evils like these.
Were these things written for nothing? Did they not know that at every time many would walk in God’s house whose hearts were not upright toward one another?
Whoever wants to recognize evils like these and understand their repayment—look, they are written in the Psalms, which say of the people who committed them, “May death come down
upon them; let them go down alive into Hades.” Do not twist what we are saying. For the saints in God’s house who are distressed and find fault are different.

or about Judas alone: “The one who eats my bread with me has lifted his heel against me,” or, “He used to eat with me at meals,”

Because of theft and betrayal. His hand was in the dish with God while he was ready to betray him. But let us fear Gehenna,
and let us be ashamed before ourselves, we who have received the name of God's greatness [?]. Let us keep ourselves holy,
free from the deeds of Judas in the house of God. For that man committed still greater evils, since it was after he received the bread that Satan entered him.

This great wrath rightly came down upon him, in keeping with the wickedness of his deeds, because instead of being cleansed of Satan by receiving some of the bread that the Lord broke and gave him, Satan entered him all the more.
This, then, is how he quickly crossed over to the other side: instead of becoming an apostle, he became a devil.
You see that anyone who makes room within himself for the unclean spirit after receiving grace, after receiving the name, after putting on the habit,
will fall into the hands of many evils. Or did we not leave the home of our worldly life in order not to sin? And where will these deeds of darkness and perversity,
these thorns and thistles, come from to entangle us? Or will we become entangled in them through our foolishness and our negligence, which have made bitter things sweet to us?
I am speaking of impurities, defilements, and sexual immorality of every kind, which are far removed from the rules of honorable marriage and foreign to the pure marriage bed, and of envy,
hatred, slander, greed for more, favoritism in judgment, and all the other things with which we have filled God's place, becoming traps for us,
and snares, and stones and pits, so that we become entangled in them, stumble over them, and fall into them.
Who else is responsible for separating what is holy from what is defiled, and what is evil from what is good, as the person in God's house is?
For whatever those who desire good see us doing, they will do; and whatever evildoers see us doing, they will do,
and they will go even further. It is not only a defiled person, distinguished from a holy person, who is unclean,
nor is what is defiled merely an animal unfit to be offered as a sacrifice to the Lord, distinguished from what is pure according to the commandments.
Rather, every evil, from crooked judgments to hypocrisy, is unclean. And anyone who touches these things—that is, does them—unless he keeps himself away from them,
will be unclean before God, just as all sins are impurities before truly godly people. Indeed, this is how unjust judges are called “unclean” because of their unclean deeds,
and upright judges are called “clean” because of their righteous deeds and their just judgments. It is the same with someone who disgraces a good person,
honors a wicked person, and insults a righteous person in the presence of an ungodly person:
the heart within him is unclean. Indeed, he is like someone who blocks up a spring of water.
Who will say that this is not so, except someone who has within him what God detests—pride—as it is written in the Gospel?
Or shall we entertain these arrogant thoughts—I saying, “Are you the one who will guide me?” and you saying, “Is this man the one who will teach me?”
Yet we have not mourned over our sins so that God will not cast us away from him on the day of our distress.
Or are these not human beings themselves, to whom he will say at that time, “Depart from me,” or, “I do not know who you are”?

It is no surprise if Christians suffer at the hands of pagans or heretics because they are jealous of them,
just as the Philistines made Isaac suffer because they were jealous of him, and just as all God's people have endured every hardship from the beginning until now because of all the godless people.
But it is all the more astonishing that we are jealous of one another, make one another suffer, and hand one another over to death, since we have one God.
There is another thing that harms fathers and brings ruin to children: when those in authority honor people so that they will follow them,
or appoint them to God's essential tasks, even though they hear about and know their evil deeds.
We want to know what should be done to a good person and what should be done to an evil person.

Listen, for the voice says, “[?] the one who speaks the truth in his heart has not practiced deceit with his tongue.” It says, “Everyone who is evil is despised in his sight, but he honors those who fear the Lord.”
Whoever the person is, whoever the priest is who fears God, let him guard himself against the evil deeds for which the voice rebuked Eli and his sons.
And he killed them in his anger because they did not stop committing their acts of sexual immorality.
But they also became robbers. Instead of making an offering to the Lord God first, they themselves came first. From
the things being offered as sacrifices.
this statement: “You have honored your sons more than me, so that they receive a blessing from the first portion of every sacrifice of Israel before me.” For it is truly infuriating when slaves
reach out their hands to eat first—especially wicked slaves—while their master is before them at the same table, before he has given them permission.
If you want to honor people or do them favors, honor them in your house. Do them favors with what belongs to you. The altar is not the place to win people over in this way.
Nor are the Lord's body and blood the means by which to do them favors. For what you are performing is a mystery, not a matter of eating and drinking.
Nor is it a place for a person to enter just as he is—a sexually immoral person.
And the prostitute, the adulterer, the extortioner, the thief, and the one who swears falsely—each in their own wickedness.
I have not presented these things as dreams. For it is our deeds that make these words condemn us, and they are right to do so.
Will we repent, then? Will we stop storing up wrath for ourselves on the day of wrath and the revelation of God's righteous judgment?
If evils of this kind are ours, then [?] the speaker is to blame for saying what does not exist. But if they do exist and are increasing, then those who find fault with the speaker are sinning.
For it is for Jesus' sake that we say these things—for Jesus' sake. Let us understand that the true gift a person should give their neighbor
is for each person to help their brother and companion in their needs—not only their needs in outward matters, but also in the distress caused by the devil's sins.
There are things that, whether a person vows to do them or does not bind himself by a vow to do them, are these: keeping his bed pure;
giving alms if he has worldly possessions; administering justice without favoritism; observing the fasting days according to the church's rules; giving firstfruits.
There are things that a person commits no sin by not vowing to do. For the Lord said, “Let the one who can bear it bear it.” But if he vows
to do them and does not do them, woe to him! These are: remaining a virgin, taking up your cross and following God, becoming a priest in his house, and becoming a monk.
Therefore, whoever falls away from these things or turns back from them has himself become a denier and has become a pillar of salt like Lot's wife—that is, a person with no wisdom in him.
If we say, “These words are fighting against us,” who does not fight against those whom God fights against? Is it his angel or his Holy Spirit
who speaks through them? Or is it such a small thing for a person to serve God in complete purity in his holy assemblies?
Even if you will not remain a virgin as you promised, do not become sexually debauched. Do not sleep with a male. Do not have many wives because you do not have one.
Even if you will not do deeds like those of the angels, do not do demonic deeds either. Even if the pagans will not hear of good things among you that they will admire,
and recognize that we belong to God, and also understand that the Lord is great and his power is great,
then do not let them hear of evil things among you either—evil things of a kind not even found among the other nations.
They are indeed children of the devil, so that not merely one or two defile God's temple and his ordinances, as it is written.
Rather, perhaps you will find one among many, or two among multitudes, who have not defiled God's temple and his ordinances, as it is written.
So too with the woman who says, “I am a virgin,” when she is not one. Do not have many husbands because you have no husband.
You will not suffer labor pains to bear children or nurse them. Nor should you torment yourself by bringing them into yourself in many evil ways before the time.
Nor should you throw them out, not knowing whether a dog or a sow will eat them, just as you have also failed to realize that fire and the worm will take possession of you.

If you will not have children at their proper time, do not hide them in secret places, or in a well or in the water, lest their souls and their bodies be hidden in the underworld and their names be covered in darkness.
For if you had not offered your face and your eyes to an unclean man, how could you have shown the devil your heart, revealing your thoughts and your reflections to him?
Have you not heard about the woman of whom it was said, “For all those around her are covered”?
Who preceded whom among those who came into you to plunder and strip their soul? Was it the wicked man? Or was it rather Satan?
For you are the one who has already seen the king. You are also the one who knows who became the guide for those who took the money from the house.
If those they brought in were thieves or robbers,
would they have left anything behind? The demon who never has enough of sinning is the one who deceived you. He is the one who cast a spell on you.

You were the first to make room for him within yourself. If you had not looked out at him, you would not have met him in the manner of a prostitute, nor would he have lurked in the corners, in the streets, and around your house.
You are the one who showed him the ways to come in and go out deceitfully. You are the one who hid him in their heart and their soul
and their mind, like a woman who has hidden her adulterous lover in the storerooms. And
in the corners of her house.
you are the one who brought him to the place where the money is hidden. You are the one who pointed it out to him.
Search, you foolish virgin. Look through all your possessions so that you may know what he has not taken from what belongs to you.
Your purity is the great treasure. Prayer is the bracelets and the various kinds of rings on your hands and fingers. Your walking in freedom is the anklet on your feet.
Your obedience is the earring in your ears. Humility is the hoop and the copper necklace around your neck.
Their knowledge is the ornament on their head or around their neck. Their fasts are the bridles of their body.
They are your meditations on the word of God, the lamp for your feet.
Grace is the ointment and the oil with which you anoint yourself and which you put on your head. Truth is the band that you tie around yourself. Wisdom is the cloth in which you wrap yourself.
Has he not taken all these and the other things from you? He emptied it down to the [?]. From its furnishings he took dignity, or the wholesome sense of shame in your eyes.
That woman said to her brother, “I will take hold of you and bring you into my mother's house, into the chamber of the woman who conceived me.”
Just as, then, the true virgin, who safeguards all her wealth in the good deeds she has done in her strength, prays for Jesus and his Spirit to dwell within her,
you yourself have taken hold of an enemy and brought him into your house, even into your inner storeroom. You have welcomed the unclean spirit. But the holy
and beloved one, the good Spirit, you have withdrawn from—not because he is unable to save you,
but rather because he has handed you over to the one who hates you, because you loved strangers and followed them.
I loved those who sleep with you, and you multiplied your prostitution with them. You multiplied those who are far from you, so that they might dwell in your house with you,
I am speaking about the spirit of wickedness and the rulers of the world of darkness, and also the ungodly people who have become one with you—and you are with them, you poor soul.
But their God, for his part, and their Lord Jesus—you did not leave him
[?] in your heart and in your thoughts, as it is written: “He too, when he saw you, forgot, and you did not fear him. He too will declare his righteousness.
And the wind will carry you away, together with everyone attached to you, and their deeds and their [?]. A gust of wind will sweep them away.”
Let us stop, then, while we are engaged in these deeds because of which we provoke God's fierce anger against us. How long will we go on speaking to God hypocritically,
and spreading out our hands deceitfully before the one from whom the ugliness of our deeds is not hidden?
How long will these troubles remain on the earth because of our acts of violence and all the things that none of us wants done to him, yet we ourselves do to one another?

“Remove the sins, and I will remove the sufferings, the scourges, and the afflictions from you,” says the voice that declares, “Remove these wicked things from your hearts, from before my eyes. Stop your wickedness.”
How long will we go on dishonoring ourselves alone, and disgracing ourselves along with his good things?
Who will defile or pollute the Lord's ordinances without first defiling himself and polluting his own deeds?

It is impossible for me to say a word without having to give an account for it. For this reason I tell you: there is a person reading the Scriptures or singing psalms of whom they say in heaven, “The one whose mouth deserves to be shut.”
There is a person in the holy places, also clothed in the honored name, of whom they say in heaven, “The enemy of God's houses, whose habit deserves to be torn.”
There is a person going to the altar and receiving the body and blood of the Lord, of whom they say in heaven, “The one whose hands and feet deserve to be cut off.”
There is a man, and there is a woman, whom people on earth consider lights in every kind of purity, of whom they say in heaven, “Look at these people, unclean in everything!”

There will certainly be a judgment between those who hear these words with sighing and weeping and those who hear them with grumbling and complaining—if indeed they do not hate the person who rebukes them.

What will this name and this outward appearance do for us while we are engaged in these improper deeds? It is in this saying spoken by the prophet that we will become rich: “Let the meek become a warrior.
Let the one who has no strength say, ‘I am strong.’” With whom should the meek become a warrior? Or in what should he be strong?
Let him fight for the truth and for God's judgments. Let him fight against sin. Let him be strong in opposing empty glory and hypocrisy,
and favoritism and deference to people—especially rich oppressors and godless pagans.

The person who pays no attention to his sins when he hears these words is the person who does not remember his end and the hour of his distress: he is the one who finds fault with the person who says these things.
This is the person whose thoughts wickedness and deceit have covered over among us, as it is written:
“Everything from which we gain no benefit at the time of our distress is harmful to our soul.”
In what have those who have come a great distance to this place become wiser, by making inquiries or passing judgment about possessions that have been stolen?
If someone's work is to remove specks from people's eyes that are ruining their sight, how is it not foolish for him to remove the specks and leave the beams in them?
I say this because, if I am here exposing people for having stolen possessions, or passing judgment on them,
why should I not expose them because sin has stolen them away, and pass judgment on them and show them the places where the enemy has hidden them—that is, defilement, pollution, and every sin?
The rule of this place is that we should benefit our soul, which the whole world is not worthy of. Do not let anyone come to me about a matter of this sort. I am not that kind of person.
The great prophet Moses was in the midst of the darkness and the cloud, and God spoke with him, so that nothing was hidden from him.
Yet he never spoke like this, nor did any of the other saints: “Go to [?], and you will find some stolen objects,” or, “Who took them?”
Like those who now deceive many people, although they know nothing. Instead, they said, “Every matter will be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses,”
or the stolen goods must be found with those who took them. To end every dispute, he said, “There shall be an oath by God between them.”
Instead, they said, “Every matter will be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses,” or the stolen goods must be found with those who took them.
To end every dispute, he said, “There shall be an oath by God between them.”

If Samuel told Saul, “The donkeys have been found,” what does that have to do with what you say—“Such-and-such, in such-and-such a place”—and with saying who stole some goods, rather than saying, “They have been found”? Is not saying
“They have been found” a peaceful matter? What about saying, “Look, they are over there,” or, “Who took them?”
Like those who now stir you up to hostility and other troubles, as you rummage through the houses of those whom they told you were the ones who took the objects,
while you gain nothing but lies, fighting, and hatred toward one another.
But because we have spoken of joy and have heard of joy, I will finish with these things. The God of all mercy
will make us worthy of these two things, so that we may share in the whole, namely: that he protect the innocent among his people,
and that he also turn us sinners away from every kind of lawlessness, and not hide his face from us from today onward, from the day we resolved in our hearts to keep his words.
so that we too may hear this encouragement.
And again: “I will make a covenant of peace with them, and they shall have a covenant of peace, and I will establish them
and multiply them, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever, and my dwelling shall be over them.”
And again: “I will bring back Jacob’s captives, and I will have mercy on the whole house of Israel.” And again: “From this time onward, I will no longer leave them in that place,”
speaking of the land of their enemies. “And I will not hide my face from them, because I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel,” says Adonai, the Lord.
I said these things knowing that you wanted to hear them. Indeed, I remember how I saw your tears flowing over your cheeks when this least of men
said this: “When we climb up onto the chair or the throne to read to those who listen to the word of God in his churches—or rather, when we go down into pits.”
And again: “What wisdom does a shepherd have if he draws water and gives a flock of sheep a drink, but does not give his own lamb a drink?”
Or someone who has lit many lamps in the house for others, but does not light his own in his room.
